title: Fib Rolling
statement: Implement `solve(n)`. Return the `n`th Fibonacci number with `F(0) = 0` and `F(1) = 1`. If `n` is negative, return the string `error`. Use an iterative rolling pair or an equivalent linear loop. Do not use the exponential double recursion.
hints: Handle 0, 1, and negatives before the loop.
Keep the previous two numbers and advance n-1 times from 1.
The naive recursive fib recomputes overlapping calls. Do not write it.

approaches.name: Rolling pair
approaches.explanation: The recurrence needs only two predecessors.

editorial: The recurrence needs only two predecessors. Rolling them forward is linear time and constant space. Memoized recursion is also linear and spends stack and a cache. The exponential tree is the version that times out for modest n.
